name: release-agent-amendment-decision
body:
Decision record for the AMENDMENT adding the optional `release-agent` to the in-flight `agent-builder-roster-cleanup` change-set.

SOURCE. The coordinator's AMEND brief: add an optional, per-repo `release-agent` the agent-builder scaffolds and the navigator dispatches ONLY after explicit user consent, granted the release-adjacent git ops (`git tag` + `git push`, branch + tags) plus repo-specific release-artefact writes (interviewed per repo like the build gates). It fills the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. This is a deliberate carve-out of the recurring push/tag law; the binary itself still never pushes/tags. The grant's value was later corrected to `ask` — see CORRECTION.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE BRANCH GRAPH. All three edited surfaces resolve as real `docs` File nodes — `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (434 lines), `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` (584 lines), `AGENTS.md` (883 lines) — so `implemented-by` targets resolve and NO planned Implementation node is needed for them. `requirements.stakeholder.agent-suite-maintainer` already contains the roster requirement (`agent-builder-drops-optional-coordinator`); the three domain entities (`generated-agent-set`, `distributed-agent-set`, `agent-file-migration`) are children of `domain.group.agent-roster`. No `release`-named domain or solution node existed.

SPINE. Added `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent` (feature `agent-builder-roster-cleanup`) under `requirements.stakeholder.agent-suite-maintainer`; a new child entity `domain.entity.release-agent-flow` (kind `entity`) under `domain.group.agent-roster`, consistent with its three siblings; and the law `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out` (`attaches-to` the new requirement). Edges: stakeholder ⊃ requirement —drives→ entity —realised-by→ the three reused components —(existing implemented-by)→ `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`. [with user: the carve-out itself]

DIVERGENCE FOUND AND RECONCILED [autonomous]. `solution.constraint.agent-builder-roster-truthful` (attached to `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt`) asserted "Its generated set is implementers only". The optional `release-agent` contradicts that absoluteness, so I amended the constraint body to admit the optional release-agent (mode `subagent` / `hidden` / `generated`), to name its push/tag `ask` carve-out, and to keep the coordinator/reviewer prohibitions intact. Leaving it unmodified would have left the spec self-contradictory.

COMPONENT REUSE [autonomous]. Reused `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt`, `solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt`, and `solution.component.agent-roster-docs` rather than creating new components: all three are already implemented-by exactly the files this change-set edits. `agent-roster-docs` is implemented-by BOTH `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`; `README.md` is edited by the sibling requirement `reviewer-is-distributed-not-generated` (item 7), so reusing it forces no fake task. All three components are already in scope via `domain.entity.distributed-agent-set`, so this amendment adds no NEW coverage gap — the release-agent's per-file edits are additional tasks over already-covered files. This is the same honest-coverage reasoning recorded in `solution.note.agent-roster-narrow-owners`.

SCOPE. The amendment edits three docs/product-source surfaces only. It does NOT edit `.opencode/agents/**` (consumer artifacts) and adds NO tests. The binary-side "never shells out to the git CLI" statements and `scripts/release.sh`'s "never pushes" behaviour stay true and are not behaviourally changed; their wording is corrected by the second amendment (see CORRECTION). The `agent-builder-main-flow` requirement/constraint prose about the agent-builder's OWN grants (read-only git + add/commit, never push/tag) remains accurate for the agent-builder and is left as-is; the carve-out constraint is the spec's scoped statement of the push/tag law.

CORRECTION [with coordinator — second amendment]. The first amendment's live nodes described the release-agent's push/tag grant as `allow` (autonomous once invoked) and left every other generated agent on `ask`. Both are wrong: the release-agent's grant is `ask` (each push/tag command prompts for human approval), it is the ONLY generated agent granted push/tag at all, every other generated agent gets no push/tag grant (denied by deny-by-default), and the law's name is "push/tag remain human-approved acts". The live nodes were corrected: `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent`, `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`, `solution.constraint.agent-builder-roster-truthful`, `domain.entity.release-agent-flow`, `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-main-flow`, `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt`, and this note. The new requirement `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only` covers the phrasing sweep and the release-only/`ask` model, driving `domain.entity.release-agent-flow` and reaching the new narrow `solution.component.push-tag-policy-surfaces` (the binary-doc/test surfaces) alongside the three reused agent-policy components; see `requirements.note.push-tag-human-approved-correction`.
